body:
Stable release. A computer that ran v1.8.1 runs v2.0.0 as it is: the settings file, the presets, the MCP tools and the command line carry over, and a program on the *Stable* update channel offers this version by itself.

## A new interface

The window has been redrawn: flat surfaces in the dark and light themes, a new set of line icons compiled into the program, a new application icon, Segoe UI Semibold titles, and CJK text sized to sit evenly beside the Latin letters.

- **Get started page.** While nothing is open, the preview shows the three steps (choose the source, adjust DLSS 5, save) and a tile for each way in: *Live from VRChat* (with whether a Spout sender is there), *Open a picture* and *Open a video*.
- **One Advanced switch**, at the top of the sidebar beside the search field. It shows everything beyond the essentials: the tone and structure sliders, the neural pass resolution and output blend, *Neural pass only for captures*, the *Frame guidance* and *DLAA pre-pass* sections, V-Sync and the processing rate cap, *Internals* with its timers, and the pass timings in the status bar. It stays on by default; off, the sidebar keeps what a first picture needs.
- **Folding.** A click on a section's title folds it. The sidebar and the library fold with a click on the gap beside them (a small arrow shows the direction); the thin line at the gap's edge still resizes them.
- **Top bar and status bar.** The top bar holds the source switch with a badge for its state, a *DLSS 5* badge while the neural pass runs, undo, redo, the history, help, the language and the main action. The status bar names what is open with its size and frame rate, the progress and time left of a running job, and the file saved last, with a button that shows it in Explorer.
- **Application icon.** A sphere split down the middle: on the left the low-poly facets of a game picture, on the right the smooth light DLSS 5 gives it, lit from the upper right, framed by the corners of a camera's viewfinder. The small sizes are drawn for their size rather than scaled down, and the same mark sits in the top bar, in *About* and on the start-up card.
- **Library.** Empty, it is a single row with *Add files…* and *Add folder…*. A thumbnail shows its tick box and a ✕ (remove from the library) under the mouse; *Select all* and *Select none* are in the **…** menu. In a narrow window the header's buttons shrink to icons, and those that no longer fit move into the **…** menu.
- **Every label fits**, in all four languages and down to the narrowest sidebar and the 720 × 480 minimum window: long names wrap instead of being cut, a control too wide for its row moves below its label, a button pair that no longer fits side by side is stacked, and a file name such as `config.json` is never broken at its dot.
- **Reset icons.** The ↺ beside a slider shows only once its value differs from the default, and fades in and out without moving the slider; it resets that one value. The *Frame guidance* sliders (search radius, confidence threshold, depth update interval, cut threshold) have it now too, and the zoom row's ↺ shows only when the view is zoomed or moved.
- **Search** looks through every control, with the Advanced switch off too, and a result no longer shows a badge or a caption without the control it belongs to; *Skin structure strength* is now found by its name.
- **Setup guide.** Its pages are tall enough for the longest one in all four languages; in a small window a page that scrolls fades out at its edge instead of ending in a half-cut line, and the settings page now says that the language is chosen in the top bar.
- The Spout state reads the same everywhere: *No Spout sender found* while no sender runs, *Waiting for VRChat Spout stream…* while senders run but the chosen one has sent no picture yet.
- The overlay info no longer runs under the picture's tool row, *Internals* shows its timers as a table, and the MCP key rows keep their buttons aligned.

## Lighter on the computer

- While nothing on the screen changes, the window redraws only a few times a second, and at full rate again for a moment after any input.
- The live camera is processed only when the sender has a new frame. A sender that does not count its frames is tested with a small hash on the GPU (on a device of its own, outside the processing queue); on the test machine the live mode's CPU load fell from most of one core to 5–7 % of it.
- The depth network is loaded only while DLSS 5, DLAA or the depth view needs it, and the font files are mapped instead of copied into memory: started with DLSS 5 off, the program now takes about 560 MB instead of about 1.1 GB.

## Linux package

`VRChatDLSS5Cam-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` runs the program on Linux with an NVIDIA card (GeForce RTX 20 to 50, NVIDIA driver 5xx or newer). It is the Windows program run under Proton through [umu-launcher](https://github.com/Open-Wine-Components/umu-launcher): unpack, `./vrchat-dlss5-cam`, and the first start fetches GE-Proton and the Steam Linux Runtime into your home folder (about 2.5 GB, once). `./install-linux.sh` adds a menu entry. Nothing is installed system-wide and Steam is not required. Tested on a Steam Deck running Ubuntu 26.04 with an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER as an external card.

What works: pictures with the neural pass, depth and DLSS super resolution; videos and animated images as input (GPU decoding); WebP, GIF, APNG and PNG-sequence output; MCP server, remote access, updates, mirror sites, all four languages. Not available under Proton: Live mode (Spout senders exist only on Windows), MP4 output (no H.264/HEVC encoder: a video that would come back as MP4 is saved as WebP at the WebP quality set in the sidebar), NVIDIA optical flow (the FSR optical flow takes over by itself), and the Radeon edition. `docs/LINUX.md` has the details, the command line, and the troubleshooting list.

The program now recognises Proton: the sidebar explains the missing Live mode and MP4 output where they would be, the video output list offers the four formats that exist there, and the log names the Wine and kernel versions. The package carries Microsoft's Direct3D shader compiler (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, a Windows SDK redistributable) because Proton's own compiler gets the picture's alpha wrong; the compiled shaders are cached in the data folder (`data/shaders`), on Windows too, so starts after the first skip the compiler. Proton has none of the Windows fonts, so the program uses Proton's own (Liberation Sans for Segoe UI, Source Han Sans and Ume Gothic for Chinese, Japanese and Korean) at the Windows fonts' sizes: the layout is the same as on Windows.

## MCP

- `vdc_submit` accepts `job_id`: the input of an earlier job of the same key is processed again with another look, so a client tunes a picture without uploading it again.
- A job reports **Done** only after its output file has been written; a client that fetched the result the moment the job finished could read a half-written file before.
- The AstrBot plugin has left this repository and is published separately.

## Fixes

- Values given on the command line (`--set`, `--lang`, the folder of `--process`) held for that run and were then written into `settings.ini` as if chosen in the sidebar, so a `--set` in a shortcut or in a bot's script changed the program's own settings for every later start. They now hold for that run only; a value changed again during the run, in the sidebar or through MCP, is saved as before.
- A window screenshot (`--screenshot`) or an MCP preview saved to a file no longer locks the settings while it is written; only captures and video runs do.
- A `--headless` run given `--exit-after` and no `--process` stays for that time; it ended after three seconds as a run without work.

## Files

| Computer | File |
|---|---|
| Windows, GeForce RTX 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` |
| Windows, AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` |
| Linux with an NVIDIA card (runs under Proton) | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (see `docs/LINUX.md`) |
name: v2.0.0 — Stable release: a new interface, lighter when idle, Linux package, command-line fixes

body:
Two downloads: `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` (GeForce) and `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition). Chat bots built on AstrBot also get `astrbot_plugin_vdc.zip`.

The first stable release since v1.7.0: it carries everything from the v1.8.0 pre-release (the MCP server with remote access, keys and a job queue, and the FSR optical flow; a summary is at the end) plus the changes below.

## MCP

- **Every tool is named `vdc_...`** (`vdc_get_status`, `vdc_open`, `vdc_submit`, `vdc_jobs`, ...), so a client that has several MCP servers never mixes them up. The names of v1.8.0, without the prefix, still answer.
- **`vdc_submit` takes `preset: "default"`** for the program's default look, so a bot needs no saved preset.
- **A job says which upload it came from** (`uploadId` in its JSON), so a bridge can match results to its own uploads.
- The server's guidance and its error texts name the tools with the prefix.

## Chat bots: a plugin for AstrBot

A chat model sees the picture a person posts, but it cannot hand the picture's bytes to a tool. The repository now ships a plugin for [AstrBot](https://astrbot.app) (`integrations/astrbot/astrbot_plugin_vdc`, also `astrbot_plugin_vdc.zip` below) that closes the gap:

- before the model answers, the pictures and videos of the message are uploaded to the server and the model is told the upload ids, so it only has to call `vdc_submit` with one of them;
- the plugin watches the jobs made from its uploads and posts the finished picture or video into the chat by itself; the model only relays the queue message;
- `/vdc` processes a picture without any model, `/vdc status` and `/vdc jobs` show the server and the queue; **Queue every uploaded picture at once** needs no MCP setup at all, and two model tools of the plugin's own (`vdc_queue`, `vdc_post_result`) cover a model that has no MCP tools.

Setup and settings: docs/MCP.md ("Chat bots: the AstrBot plugin") and the plugin's README (English and Chinese).

## Since v1.7.0 (the v1.8.0 pre-release)

- **MCP server.** MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, chat bots and others) drive the program through the same actions as the window: 26 tools and 8 resources, Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:51550/mcp` or the stdio bridge `--mcp`. Sidebar section *MCP*; everything is in docs/MCP.md.
- **Other computers: reach, keys and roles.** *Reach* chooses between this computer only and the local network; keys with the viewer, jobs and admin roles (`mcp-keys.json`); a button adds the firewall rule.
- **A job queue for bots that share one machine.** Upload, submit (it answers at once with the place in the queue, an estimate and a message to relay), a long-poll wait, downloads, per-key and global caps with a retry time, fairness between keys, persistence across restarts and a retention time. `--headless` keeps the program alive as a server.
- **FSR optical flow.** The program's own optical flow in the shape of the FidelityFX one, on any card: the Radeon edition's motion source now (block matching before) and the GeForce edition's fallback when NVIDIA Optical Flow is unavailable, with frame guidance controls (search radius, bidirectional check).
- Fix: `--set`, presets, per-file parameters and undo steps no longer reset the motion, depth and auto-reset choices.

## Documentation

docs/MCP.md uses the prefixed names and gained the AstrBot section; the four READMEs point to the plugin.
name: v1.8.1 — Stable release: MCP tools prefixed vdc_, a plugin for AstrBot chat bots

body:
**Pre-release.** Please try it and report problems in the issues. The stable channel keeps v1.7.0 until this version is promoted.

Two downloads: `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` (GeForce edition) and `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition).

## MCP server

- **MCP clients can drive the program.** A built-in [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server lets Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients open pictures and videos, change every setting, look at the preview, save captures, run the library and read the log, with the same checks and the same undo history as the sidebar. It is off by default; the new sidebar section *MCP* turns it on, shows the address, copies the client configuration, and can put the server in a read-only mode where clients may look but not change anything.
- **26 tools** (`get_status`, `describe_settings`, `get_settings`, `set_settings`, `reset_settings`, `open`, `open_live`, `list_senders`, `close_media`, `library`, `process`, `capture`, `cancel`, `video`, `preview`, `wait`, `undo`, `redo`, `history`, `presets`, `get_log`, `window`, `reload`, `upload`, `submit`, `jobs`) and **8 resources** (status, settings, settings schema, library, log, jobs, the preview and the window as PNG). `preview` answers with the picture as the display shows it (output, original, wipe, motion vectors or depth), scaled to a `max_edge` of the client's choice, and can save the full-size picture too.
- **Other computers can use it: reach, keys and roles.** The *Reach* control chooses between *This computer only* (loopback, as before) and *Local network*. Off loopback a key is mandatory: keys are created in the sidebar with a name and one of three roles - *viewer* (look only), *jobs* (send files, take the own results) and *admin* (everything the window can do) - and are sent as a bearer token, as a `?key=` query on the HTTP pages, or through the stdio bridge (`VRChatDLSS5Cam.exe --mcp --mcp-url http://<host>:51550/mcp --mcp-key <key>`) for clients that only launch a command. The sidebar shows every LAN address, each key's last use and call count, and an *Allow through Windows Firewall* button adds the inbound rule with one click. Keys live in `mcp-keys.json` next to the settings.
- **A job queue for bots that share one machine.** Several chat bots pointing at one GPU do not wait in the dark: `upload` (base64) or a streamed `POST /upload` or a URL brings the file in, `submit` chooses a preset and per-job overrides and answers *at once* with the queue position, how many are ahead, an estimate learned from earlier runs and a plain sentence the bot can relay ("Queued at position 3 ..."). Jobs are scheduled fairly across keys, a global queue limit and a per-key limit answer with `retryAfterSeconds` instead of piling up, `jobs wait` long-polls up to a minute, `jobs result` returns the finished picture inline (or a download link for videos), `jobs cancel` and `jobs delete` do what they say, and results are kept for a configurable number of hours and then swept. A queued job never blocks the person at the window: their own work runs first and the bot is told so. Jobs survive a restart of the program. A running job locks the interface like a batch and shows in the lock banner and the top badge.
- **Runs as a server.** `--headless` with the server switched on keeps the program alive without a window; the advanced controls (queue limits, upload limit, "this computer needs no key", job folder) sit behind the global *Advanced* toggle so the section stays short. See [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md) for a step-by-step guide, the tool table and a minimal Python bot.
- **Two ways to connect.** Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:51550/mcp` (`claude mcp add --transport http vrchat-dlss5-cam http://127.0.0.1:51550/mcp`), or the stdio bridge `VRChatDLSS5Cam.exe --mcp` for clients that launch a command: it talks to the running program, or starts it when it is not running. `--mcp-port <port>` serves one session on a chosen port. See [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md).
- The interface stays the same on the way: the tools run between the frames of the interface thread and set the same events the widgets set, so a change by the client shows the same toast, records the same undo step and is saved the same way.

## FSR optical flow

- **A new motion source that runs on any card.** *FSR optical flow* is this program's own optical flow, in the shape of the optical flow of the AMD FidelityFX SDK (MIT): a luma pyramid of up to six levels, the coarsest level finds the large motion, every level below refines what it inherits, a median over whole vectors runs between the levels, and the finest level is searched once more in the opposite direction so that vectors which do not lead back lose their confidence. It follows fast motion far better than block matching (about 0.3 ms at 2560x1440 on an RTX 5090, 0.3 ms at 1280x720 on an RX 9060 XT).
- **Radeon edition: the FSR optical flow is now the motion source.** Radeon has no hardware optical flow engine; earlier versions used block matching there. Settings files that still had the hardware engine selected move to the FSR flow once.
- **GeForce edition:** NVIDIA Optical Flow stays the default. When the engine is unavailable the app now falls back to the FSR optical flow instead of block matching.
- **Frame guidance controls:** the new mode in the *Motion vectors* list, *Search radius* (the full search of the coarsest level; one pixel there stands for 2^(levels-1) pixels of the picture), *Bidirectional consistency check*, and a status line with the level count.

## Fixes

- `--set`, presets, per-file parameters and undo steps no longer reset the motion, depth and auto-reset choices to the defaults: the migration of 0.1.x settings files now runs only when a whole settings file is loaded.

## Documentation

- READMEs in all four languages: the feature list, the Radeon expectations, the settings table, troubleshooting and the design section describe the FSR optical flow.
name: v1.8.0 — Pre-release: FSR optical flow, MCP server with remote access, keys and a job queue

body:
## Animated pictures are processed like videos

- Animated **GIF**, **APNG** and **animated WebP** files open as sequences and go through the same neural pass as videos: preview with seeking, in/out range, hover thumbnails, the batch queue and the media library.
- **Match the source** keeps the format, the loop count and every frame's duration. Otherwise *Save as* offers MP4, PNG sequence, GIF, APNG and WebP for any source, so an MP4 can become a GIF and a GIF an MP4.
- Transparency is kept for GIF, APNG and WebP outputs when the source has it and *Keep transparency* is on. The sidebar's status line shows format, frame count, loop count and transparency.
- New setting: **WebP quality** (50-100, 100 = lossless). Still WebP pictures also decode when the system has no WIC codec for them.
- Limits worth knowing: GIF delays are centiseconds with a 2 cs minimum (so a 60 fps source becomes 50 fps), and GIF holds 256 colours per frame with 1-bit transparency.

## Output file names

- The saved files' names come from a template. Tokens: `{name}`, `{date}`, `{time}`, `{size}`, `{width}`, `{height}`, `{insize}`, `{inwidth}`, `{inheight}`. Everything else is kept as typed, characters a file name cannot hold become `_`, and a name already taken gets `_2`, `_3`, …
- Live captures and processed files have their own template, shown in the Capture section for the current mode: *File name* (default `VRChat_DLSS5_{date}_{time}_{size}`) and *Output file name* (default `{name}_DLSS5_{size}`). An empty box means the default it shows. An image sequence's folder follows the template as well.
- On the command line: `--set captureName=…` and `--set outputName=…`.

## Fixes

- **DLAA presets**: every preset the NGX interface names (Default, A-O) is offered again and passed to the runtime as chosen. The earlier build re-mapped anything outside J-N to K before the runtime saw it, which looked like the preset could not be chosen.
- **8K video output**: an MP4 above H.264 level 5.2 (a 4K video upscaled to 7680x4320 at 60 fps) failed with "no H.264 encoder is available", because the level was missing from the media type. It is now set from the macroblock rate, and a stream the encoders still refuse is retried as HEVC before the run reports a clear size error.
- A failed run left the writer's failure flag set, so every later run ended at once with the same error until the app was restarted. The writers are reset when a run starts.
- **Match the source** now scales the bitrate with the picture, so a 4K file upscaled to 8K is no longer written at its original bitrate, and a matched output past 4096 pixels a side is written as HEVC, which the hardware encoders accept.
- A neural pass capped below the picture while DLSS super resolution was on was fed the full-size picture, so the network saw only the top left corner blown over the whole frame.
- The wheel over a list opened in the sidebar scrolled the sidebar away underneath the open list. A list now keeps the wheel for itself.
- A portrait picture upscaled to 8K could not be fitted into the preview: the magnification stopped at 10 % of the picture's pixels, above what the fitted view needs in a small window. The floor is now the fitted view whenever that is smaller.
- The advanced readouts (GPU time, processed frames, neural pass size, output change, estimate) share one right-aligned value column, the mirror-site block fades in like the other panels, and the shader warnings logged at every start are gone.

## Known limitation

At 7680x4320 the DLSS 5 runtime can answer a near-black frame carrying white text with flashing colour blocks although it reports success. Moving pictures come out clean.

## Downloads

- `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` — GeForce edition (RTX 20 and newer, DLSS 5 runtimes bundled).
- `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` — Radeon edition (FSR host for [DLSS-NR-on-AMD](https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD); the port's installer is downloaded from its own release page, never bundled).

libwebp 1.6.0 (BSD-3) is now linked into the application; its licence ships in `licenses/`.
name: v1.7.0 — Stable release: animated pictures processed like videos, output file names

body:
## Radeon edition: DLSS-NR-on-AMD through the mirror site

- With **GitHub access** set to a mirror site or to a site of your own, the Radeon edition now looks up the latest [DLSS-NR-on-AMD](https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD) release and downloads its installer through that site as well. GitHub itself remains the fallback when the site does not deliver.
- The release entry comes from `port.json`, which this repository refreshes at every release and once a day.
- The download line names the site in use.
- On a first start the look-up waits for the setup guide, where you choose how GitHub is reached.

## Downloads

- `VRChatDLSS5Cam-v1.6.1-win64.zip` — GeForce edition (RTX 20 and newer, DLSS 5 runtimes bundled).
- `VRChatDLSS5Cam-v1.6.1-win64-amd.zip` — Radeon edition (FSR host for DLSS-NR-on-AMD; the port's installer is downloaded from its own release page, never bundled).
name: v1.6.1 — Stable release: DLSS-NR-on-AMD through the GitHub mirror site

body:
**Stable release.** A setup guide at the first start, a mirror option for the update check where GitHub is hard to reach, and a mode switch that animates the whole window; verified on a GeForce RTX 5090, both editions carry the changes. This is the new stable release; v1.5.3 remains available below it.

### Which file to download

| Graphics card | File |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` |
| AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition) |

The Radeon edition fetches DLSS-NR-on-AMD's installer for you at the first start (nothing of the port is bundled; it is downloaded from its own release page https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD/releases). What to expect on Radeon is listed in the README under *AMD Radeon cards*.

### New in v1.6.0

- **Setup guide.** The first start opens a short guide: language and theme, how the program reaches GitHub, what the main controls do, and where to find the guide, the documentation and the search box afterwards. Existing installs see it once at their next start. *About > Setup guide* opens it again at any time; when it closes, the sidebar moves to the About section and the documentation and guide buttons light up once. The last page has a *Star on GitHub* and a *Like on BOOTH* button.
- **GitHub access with mirror sites.** In some regions (mainland China, for one) GitHub is slow or unreachable, so the update check could not run. *About > GitHub access* now offers *GitHub directly*, *Mirror sites, the fastest one* (eight relay sites are measured and the fastest is used; *Measure the sites* shows the times) or *A mirror site of my own*. Through a mirror the check reads a release manifest (`updates.json` in the repository, kept current by a workflow) instead of the GitHub API. When no site answers, a popup offers the other options.
- **The mode switch animates the whole window.** Switching between live, picture and video now fades the sidebar, the media library and the status bar together with the picture instead of only the picture.
- **Honest status lines before a picture is loaded.** The optical-flow and depth-estimator lines used to report *Not available* until the first frame arrived; they now read *waiting for a picture, it starts with the first frame*.
- **DLAA presets.** Only *Default* and presets J to N are offered; the other presets no longer produce a result with the current runtime.
- **Sidebar labels are no longer cut at the right edge.** Long control names (Japanese, English) used to run past the sidebar; the label column now takes the width of the widest label in the current language, a status line wraps, and a row of buttons (or the *Advanced* switch) moves to the next line when it has no room.
- **The experimental NGX core route is gone.** The driver refused the neural pass on it; the host route is the only one.
- **No host-route control any more.** Each edition has exactly one way to run the neural pass: the GeForce edition hosts `nvngx_dlssnr.dll` itself, the Radeon edition runs the FSR host that DLSS-NR-on-AMD attaches to. The *Host route* control under *Advanced* is gone (the Radeon edition used to fall back to the direct route on a card that is not a Radeon), and each edition points to the other one when it finds the other vendor's card.
- Version 1.6.0 for both editions.

Previous stable release: [v1.5.3](https://github.com/AlanBacker/VRChat-DLSS5-Cam/releases/tag/v1.5.3).
name: v1.6.0 — Stable release: setup guide, GitHub mirror sites, whole-window mode animation

body:
**Stable release.** Two fixes for the depth view of a still picture and for a runtime path that no longer exists; verified on a GeForce RTX 5090, both editions carry the changes. This is the new stable release; v1.5.0 to v1.5.2 remain available below it.

### Which file to download

| Graphics card | File |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` |
| AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition) |

The Radeon edition fetches DLSS-NR-on-AMD's installer for you at the first start (nothing of the port is bundled; it is downloaded from its own release page https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD/releases). What to expect on Radeon is listed in the README under *AMD Radeon cards*.

### Fixed in v1.5.3

- **A still picture's depth estimate is captured once the estimator is ready.** With *Depth: estimated* on, a picture gets a fixed number of neural passes to settle. The depth estimator starts only after the neural pass has been created and then needs a few seconds to build its session (1.5 to 5 s on an RTX 5090), so with a fast card the passes were used up before it was ready: no estimate was ever taken, the depth view stayed black and the overlay reported *Depth: zero* although the estimator itself was fine. When the estimator becomes ready and no estimate has been captured yet, the program now runs a further round of passes (up to twice per picture; the log says "Still passes: 24 more"). A save of that picture waits for the estimator instead of writing the file without depth, bounded at 20 s.
- **A runtime path whose file is gone no longer blocks the neural pass.** A file set under *DLSS 5 runtime path* that has since been deleted or moved (an old unpacked folder, say) made the program report the runtime as missing even though the download contains both builds. The bundled build is now used instead, the log names both files, and a note under the path field says so; clearing the path ends the note.
- Version 1.5.3 for both editions.

Previous stable release: [v1.5.0](https://github.com/AlanBacker/VRChat-DLSS5-Cam/releases/tag/v1.5.0). What v1.5.1 and v1.5.2 added (audio track choice, automatic restart after a loss of the graphics device, DLSS super resolution to a custom output size, the size limits of the NVIDIA features handled, one neural pass resolution list, the way back to the stable channel, runtime fallback fix) is part of this release too.
name: v1.5.3 — Stable release: still-picture depth estimate, missing runtime path handled

body:
**Pre-release.** DLSS super resolution to a custom output size, the limits of the NVIDIA features handled, a simpler resolution section, and the way back to the stable channel; verified on a GeForce RTX 5090, both editions carry the changes. It becomes the stable release once it has proven itself in use; the stable release stays v1.5.0 until then.
预发布版：新增 DLSS 超分辨率到自定义输出尺寸、处理 NVIDIA 功能的尺寸上限、简化分辨率设置、可退回稳定版；已在 RTX 5090 上验证，两个版本均包含这些改动。确认无问题后再转为正式版，在此之前正式版仍是 v1.5.0。

### Which file to download / 下载哪个文件

| Graphics card / 显卡 | File / 文件 |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` |
| AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition / Radeon 版) |

The Radeon edition fetches DLSS-NR-on-AMD's installer for you at the first start (nothing of the port is bundled; it is downloaded from its own release page https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD/releases). What to expect on Radeon is listed in the README under *AMD Radeon cards*.
Radeon 版会在首次启动时为你下载 DLSS-NR-on-AMD 的安装器（不捆绑该项目的任何文件，只从其自己的发布页下载）；Radeon 上的预期表现见 README 的 *AMD Radeon 显卡* 一节。

### New in v1.5.2

- **DLSS super resolution to a custom output size.** With *Custom output resolution* on and an output larger than the source, the picture is upscaled by DLSS itself (NVIDIA's official super resolution, GeForce edition): the render size is chosen from the modes DLSS offers for that output, and the DLSS 5 neural pass then runs at the output size. 1080p to 4K, 1440p to 8K and similar are now real upscales rather than resampling. The *Upscaling method* combo keeps plain resampling (Catmull-Rom) as the alternative, and it is what the Radeon edition uses. A warning under the control says how many times more pixels every later stage has to process: super resolution to 4K or 8K costs a lot of speed and video memory, so on a live stream set a processing rate cap.
- **The limits of the NVIDIA features are handled.** DLSS accepts outputs up to 8192 pixels a side, and the DLSS 5 runtime creates its pass up to about 45 megapixels (measured on an RTX 5090 with runtime 310.8: 7680×5760 works, 6912×6912 is refused). A 3072×5504 picture super-resolved to 7680×13760 hit both and the program reported the runtime as broken. Larger outputs are now finished within those limits and resampled to the requested size; the Source section says so ("finished at 4608×8192 and resampled to 7680×13652"). If the runtime still refuses a size, the pass is created again smaller instead of failing, and DLAA is switched off with a hint for outputs above the limit. The READMEs name the limits.
- **One neural pass resolution list.** The mode selector, percentage slider and long-edge cap are replaced by one list: full resolution, long-edge caps from 3840 down to 720, or 75 / 50 / 25 %. The default stays the full resolution.
- **The way back to the stable channel.** A pre-release that switches the update channel to *Stable* is now offered the newest stable release even though it is older, with the same card and one-click install as an update. Changing the channel checks at once.
- **Runtime fallback fixed.** A DLSS 5 build was declared broken and dropped for the session after any failure, which on an RTX 4080 ended with no runtime left ("DLSSNR CreateFeature failed (FeatureNotSupported)" on a plain 8K picture). A build now counts as failed only when it does not load or its feature cannot be created; once every build has been tried, the card's own build is loaded again. The experimental in-feature neural upscaling (*nrUpscale*) is removed: the runtime's evaluate refused every ratio.
- Hidden setting `nrPassBudgetMp` (settings file only): a lower starting pixel budget for the neural pass on cards short of memory.

### 简体中文

- **DLSS 超分辨率到自定义输出尺寸。** 打开"自定义输出分辨率"并把输出设得比来源大时，画面由 DLSS 本身放大（NVIDIA 官方超分辨率，GeForce 版）：渲染尺寸从 DLSS 为该输出提供的模式里选取，随后 DLSS 5 神经渲染在输出尺寸上运行。1080p 到 4K、1440p 到 8K 现在是真正的超分而不是重采样。"放大方式"下拉仍保留插值重采样（Catmull-Rom）作为备选，Radeon 版使用的就是它。控件下方的警告会说明后续每一步要处理的像素是来源的多少倍：超分到 4K 或 8K 会大幅降低速度、增加显存占用，实时串流请设置处理帧率上限。
- **处理 NVIDIA 功能的尺寸上限。** DLSS 最大支持单边 8192 像素的输出，DLSS 5 运行库最多能建约 4500 万像素的神经渲染（RTX 5090、运行库 310.8 实测：7680×5760 可以，6912×6912 被拒绝）。一张 3072×5504 的图超分到 7680×13760 时两条都撞上了，程序报成了运行库故障。现在更大的输出会先在上限内完成，再重采样到指定尺寸；视频源区会说明（"先在 4608×8192 完成，再重采样到 7680×13652"）。运行库仍拒绝某个尺寸时，神经渲染会自动缩小后重建而不是报错；超过上限的输出会关闭 DLAA 并给出提示。README 写明了这些上限。
- **神经渲染分辨率合并为一个列表。** 模式选择、百分比滑块和长边上限合并成一个下拉：完整分辨率、长边上限 3840 到 720，或 75 / 50 / 25 %。默认仍是完整分辨率。
- **可退回稳定版。** 预发布版把更新通道切到"稳定版"后，即使最新稳定版更旧，也会以同样的卡片和一键安装提供；切换通道时立即检查。
- **运行库回退修复。** 以前 DLSS 5 的某个构建只要出一次错就被判定损坏并在本次会话中弃用，在一台 RTX 4080 上最终导致没有可用的运行库（普通 8K 图片报 "DLSSNR CreateFeature failed (FeatureNotSupported)"）。现在只有加载失败或建不出功能才算失败；所有构建都试过后会重新加载显卡对应的构建。实验性的功能内神经上采样（nrUpscale）已移除：运行库对所有比例都拒绝。
- 隐藏设置 `nrPassBudgetMp`（仅限设置文件）：显存不足的显卡可以调低神经渲染的起始像素预算。
name: v1.5.2 — DLSS super resolution to a custom output size, size limits handled

body:
**Pre-release.** Two fixes for reports on v1.5.0, verified on a GeForce RTX 5090; both editions carry them. It becomes the stable release once it has proven itself in use; the stable release stays v1.5.0 until then.
预发布版：v1.5.0 的两个问题修复，已在 RTX 5090 上验证；确认无问题后再转为正式版，在此之前正式版仍是 v1.5.0。

### Which file to download / 下载哪个文件

| Graphics card / 显卡 | File / 文件 |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` |
| AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition / Radeon 版) |

The Radeon edition fetches DLSS-NR-on-AMD's installer for you at the first start (nothing of the port is bundled; it is downloaded from its own release page https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD/releases). What to expect on Radeon is listed in the README under *AMD Radeon cards*.
Radeon 版会在首次启动时为你下载 DLSS-NR-on-AMD 的安装器（不捆绑该项目的任何文件，只从其自己的发布页下载）；Radeon 上的预期表现见 README 的 *AMD Radeon 显卡* 一节。

### Fixed in v1.5.1

- **A video exported without sound.** An iPhone MOV carries two audio tracks: Apple's spatial audio (four channels, which Windows cannot decode) listed first, and the stereo AAC track second. The program took the first track only, could not decode it, and wrote the video silent (`log.txt`: "the audio stream cannot be decoded"). It now uses the first audio track that decodes; `log.txt` lists the tracks of the file and the one taken. Verified with that MOV on the RTX 5090: the export carries the AAC track at the same level as the source.
- **The graphics device was lost on a live stream.** On an RTX 4080 SUPER, a 1080p live stream upscaled to 4K on a card fully loaded for 12.7 minutes while VRChat rendered on the same card ended in a driver reset (`log.txt`: "Device removed", `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`) and a modal "graphics device was lost" message. The driver resets every program on the card at that moment; nothing in this program precedes it. The program now starts again by itself once the driver is back, tells you so in a notice, and keeps the log of the lost session as `log-device-loss.txt` next to `log.txt`. If the device is lost again within a minute of such a restart, or in a scripted run (`--process`, `--headless`, `--exit-after`), the message is shown and the program exits with code 2 as before. If it repeats on your card, lower the load: a processing rate cap, a lower *Neural pass resolution* or a maximum-resolution cap, the neural upscaling to the custom resolution off, or a frame rate limit in VRChat; a newer graphics driver is worth a try (README, *Troubleshooting*).
- **Video memory in the log.** The `Perf:` line every 15 s and the device-removed entry carry the video memory this process uses and the budget the system grants it, so a loss under load can be read from the log.
- **README (four languages):** troubleshooting entries for the lost graphics device and for the silent export. `COMMAND_LINE.md`: exit code 2 after a device loss and the automatic restart (`--after-device-loss` is added to the arguments of the restarted instance).

### 简体中文

- **导出的视频没有声音。** iPhone 的 MOV 有两条音轨：排在前面的是 Apple 空间音频（四声道，Windows 无法解码），其后才是立体声 AAC。程序以前只取第一条，解码失败后把视频写成了无声（`log.txt`："the audio stream cannot be decoded"）。现在改为使用第一条能解码的音轨，`log.txt` 会列出文件的各条音轨及所采用的那条。已在 RTX 5090 上用该 MOV 验证：导出带有 AAC 音轨，音量与源文件一致。
- **实时串流时图形设备丢失。** 一台 RTX 4080 SUPER 上，1080p 实时串流放大到 4K、显卡连续满载 12.7 分钟且 VRChat 在同一张卡上渲染，最终驱动重置（`log.txt`："Device removed"，`DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`），程序弹出"图形设备已丢失"后退出。驱动重置时显卡上的所有程序都会受影响，程序日志里在此之前没有任何异常。现在程序会在驱动恢复后自动重新启动并弹出提示，丢失前那次会话的日志保留为 `log.txt` 旁边的 `log-device-loss.txt`。若重启后一分钟内再次丢失，或是脚本化运行（`--process`、`--headless`、`--exit-after`），则仍显示提示并以退出码 2 结束。若在你的显卡上反复出现，请降低负载：设置处理帧率上限、调低神经渲染分辨率或限制最大分辨率、关闭神经上采样到自定义分辨率，或在 VRChat 里限制帧率；也值得试试更新显卡驱动（见 README 常见问题）。
- **日志中的显存占用。** 每 15 秒一行的 `Perf:` 和设备丢失记录现在带有本进程占用的显存和系统分配的预算，方便从日志判断满载时的情况。
- **README（四种语言）：** 新增"图形设备已丢失"和"导出的视频没有声音"两条常见问题。`COMMAND_LINE.md`：设备丢失后的退出码 2 和自动重启（重启的实例参数里会多出 `--after-device-loss`）。
name: v1.5.1

body:
**Full release.** The first since v1.2.1: everything from the v1.3.0–v1.4.5 pre-releases, verified on a GeForce RTX 5090 and (Radeon edition) on a physical Radeon RX 9060 XT.

### Which file to download / 下载哪个文件

| Graphics card / 显卡 | File / 文件 |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip` |
| AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 | `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` (Radeon edition / Radeon 版) |

The Radeon edition fetches DLSS-NR-on-AMD's installer for you at the first start (nothing of the port is bundled; it is downloaded from its own release page https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD/releases). What to expect on Radeon is listed in the README under *AMD Radeon cards*.
Radeon 版会在首次启动时为你下载 DLSS-NR-on-AMD 的安装器（不捆绑该项目的任何文件，只从其自己的发布页下载）；Radeon 上的预期表现见 README 的 *AMD Radeon 显卡* 一节。

### New in v1.5.0

- **Movable picture toolbar.** The turn / mirror / crop row over the picture has a grip on its left: drag it anywhere over the picture. Drop it past an edge, or press the arrow on its right, and it tucks away into a small tab on that edge; the tab brings it back. The place and the tucked state are kept across sessions.
- **Radeon cards and optical flow.** On a Radeon card the status line, the tooltip and the About window now say that the card has no hardware optical-flow engine (it is an NVIDIA feature) and that block matching is used, instead of a bare "not available". The README's *Optical flow unavailable* entry covers this case first.
- **Full releases reach the pre-release channel.** Someone on a pre-release build sees this full release in the update window, marked *Full release* (pre-releases are marked *Pre-release*), with a note that it replaces the pre-release build.
- **Release page:** the download table above tells GeForce and Radeon users which file is theirs.
- **README (four languages):** the download table; a new *What to expect on Radeon in this version* list (cards, what works, what is slower, what is missing); the planned Radeon optical-flow pass of this program's own, ported from the MIT-licensed optical flow of the AMD FidelityFX SDK, as a future goal.
- **Radeon: the depth network and the port no longer overlap.** DLSS-NR-on-AMD's network and the depth network (DirectML) do not share the card: a neural pass that ran alongside the estimator's warm-up stretched from 0.17 s to 2.7 s, past the driver's two-second limit, and the graphics device was lost (seen on the RX 9060 XT: a driver restart, the program to be started again). The program now waits for the estimator before every neural pass, so the two take turns; the passes of a picture start once the estimator is ready. The earlier "three-second stall of one frame in a 4K batch" was the same overlap.
- **Radeon: the strength sliders no longer re-run the passes.** On the FSR host route the preset, style and strengths up to 1 are the port's own (its overlay), so a change of them here composites the existing result at once instead of running the picture through 24 passes again, about four seconds at 4K for no change in the picture.
- **Radeon: idle load, measured.** After a picture has run its passes the card idles at about 2 % (the same as on a GeForce). One CPU core stays busy from the first neural pass on: a thread of DLSS-NR-on-AMD polls the card at full speed (its inline mode). That thread is the port's; releasing the FSR context does not end it (tried), so it is listed under *What to expect on Radeon* in the README.

### Carried over from the pre-releases since v1.2.1

- v1.3.0: both DLSS 5 (DLSSNR 310.8) runtime builds bundled under `runtimes\`, chosen automatically with a fallback.
- v1.4.0–v1.4.2: the **Radeon edition** (FSR host route for DLSS-NR-on-AMD, one-click silent install of the port with consent, edition switch), live Spout turn / mirror.
- v1.4.3–v1.4.4: the *Neural pass resolution* control with two modes, percentage or a maximum-resolution cap (issue #3).
- v1.4.5: DLSS-NR-on-AMD really runs inside the app on a physical RX 9060 XT (start-up hold for the port's hooks, `InlineWaitMs` 1000, one neural frame in flight, clean exit code).

Requires, on Radeon, DLSS-NR-on-AMD v0.2.17 from its own release page (the app offers the download).
name: v1.5.0 — Full release: movable picture toolbar, Radeon fixes

body:
**Radeon edition: DLSS-NR-on-AMD now runs its network inside the app.** Verified on a physical RX 9060 XT (720p and 4K stills, batch processing from the command line).

- **Start-up hold for the port's hooks.** The cause of "no effect on AMD": DLSS-NR-on-AMD installs its DXGI/Direct3D 12 hooks from a thread of its own about 150 ms after it loads, and this app created its device and swap chain earlier than that, so the port never saw the swap chain, never started its engine and never hooked the FidelityFX dispatch. The app now waits (up to 4 s) for the port's log to report its last interface hook before creating Direct3D 12. Only the part of that log written by the current run counts (the port appends to it run after run), and the one-time restart described below waits for the first instance's hook lines before the second instance starts.
- **Port settings adjusted for saved frames.** The port's installer writes an inline budget of 200 ms, after which a frame shows the previous frame's result; a 4K frame needs about 0.2 s on the RX 9060 XT (the first one 0.4–0.6 s). The app raises `InlineWaitMs` to 1000 in `dlssnr_on_amd.ini` after an install and, if the file still has the old value, at start-up with a one-time automatic restart. Nothing else in the file is touched.
- **One neural frame in flight** while the port is loaded, so it never skips a frame ("too many frames in flight").
- **Clean exit code with the port loaded.** The port fails fast in its own unload routine when the process exits (0xC0000409 after the app's shutdown had completed). The app now ends the process itself once everything of its own is saved and released, so scripts see the real exit code.
- Log: adapter LUIDs and the Direct3D 12 device address, to match against the port's log.
- READMEs (four languages): the Radeon edition's test status and the settings-file adjustment.

Requires DLSS-NR-on-AMD v0.2.17, downloaded from its own release page: https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD/releases (the app offers the download; the installer is never bundled).

GeForce edition: unchanged apart from the version number.

Pre-release. v1.2.1 remains the recommended full release.
name: v1.4.5 — Radeon edition: DLSS-NR-on-AMD runs on an RX 9060 XT

body:
Pre-release: the Radeon edition has still not been run on Radeon hardware by the author. Reports from an RX 7000 / 9000 card, with `log.txt`, are welcome in the issues.

**The "Neural pass resolution" control is gone.** It used to run the neural pass on a smaller picture (25 to 100 % of the input) and upscale its change onto the full-resolution picture, and the result depended heavily on where it was set (issue #3). The neural pass now always runs at the input resolution — the same picture it composites onto — so the effect no longer changes with a pass-resolution value. There is nothing to set; a settings file or preset that still carries the old value simply ignores it.

Neural upscaling to a custom resolution (the experimental option in the DLSS 5 section) is unchanged.
name: v1.4.3

body:
Pre-release: the Radeon edition has still not been run on Radeon hardware by the author. The silent install below was proven against the real installer on an RTX 5090 (where the port refuses the card and the installer's window opens, the fallback), and its mechanism — feeding the installer its answers through a pipe with no window — matches how it was driven by hand earlier. Reports from an RX 7000 / 9000 card, with `log.txt`, are welcome in the issues.

**The first install needs no window and no key press.** *Install DLSS-NR-on-AMD…* used to download the installer and open its console for you to press Enter in. It now runs the installer in the background and answers its prompts itself — accept the program folder, accept the DLL name it proposes for the executable (`version.dll`) — so a first install is one press, then the automatic restart. The installer's console output is written into `log.txt`.

**The window is kept for what needs a decision.** If the folder needs administrator rights, or the card is one the port does not support, the installer opens its own window so its message is visible. *Update to …* and *Run the installer again…* (an installed folder) also open the window, where **U** updates and **R** removes; those are real choices and are left to you.

**Under the hood.** A five-minute limit, and the run is dropped if the application is closing. The DLSS 5 section shows an *Installing…* line while it runs. Nothing of DLSS-NR-on-AMD is bundled; its installer is still downloaded from its own release page only, and the first *Install* press is the agreement to its terms (linked by *Licence*).
name: v1.4.2

body:
Pre-release: the Radeon edition has still not been run on Radeon hardware by the author. The first report from an RX 9060 XT shows the FSR host (FSR 4.1.1) and DLSS-NR-on-AMD both loaded; reports with `log.txt` (which now ends with the last lines of the port's own log) are welcome in the issues.

**The DLSS 5 section says what is installed.** The Radeon edition knew only the latest release of DLSS-NR-on-AMD and offered *Update…* even when that release was the one installed. It now records the release its installer came from (an installation made with v1.4.0 is recognised by the installer file next to the executable) and reads *DLSS-NR-on-AMD v0.2.16: loaded (version.dll) · up to date*. *Update to …* appears only when a newer release of the port is out; *Run the installer again…* runs it at any time for an update (U) or the removal (R).

**Install, then restart by itself.** When the installer has finished and the weights file is there, the application restarts on its own after a short countdown (*Restart now* / *Cancel*; not while a batch or an update is running). On a Radeon card the start-up card begins with that step. Nothing of the port is bundled: the first press of *Install DLSS-NR-on-AMD…* is the agreement to its terms (personal, non-commercial use; no redistribution or modification), which are linked next to the button (*Licence*).

**Edition switch.** The GeForce edition on a Radeon card offers *Get the Radeon edition…*, the Radeon edition on a GeForce card *Get the GeForce edition…*; `--edition geforce|amd` does the same from the command line. The other edition's archive is fetched from the release page and swapped in the way an update is.

**Diagnostics.** On the FSR host route `log.txt` lists the DLSS-NR-on-AMD files next to the executable at start and ends with the last lines of `dlssnr_on_amd.log`. The *AMD Radeon cards* section of the four READMEs describes the new flow, the overlay's *Mode* (inline / async) and where the port's log is.

body:
Pre-release: the Radeon edition has not been run on Radeon hardware by the author (no such card was available); its FSR host route was exercised on an RTX 5090 only. Reports from RX 7000 / 9000 cards with `log.txt` and DLSS-NR-on-AMD's own log are welcome.

**A Radeon edition.** `VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64-amd.zip` brings the neural pass to Radeon cards through [DLSS-NR-on-AMD](https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD), a separate project that runs DLSS 5 neural rendering on AMD hardware by attaching to programs that use FSR. The edition hosts an FSR 3.1 context (AMD's FidelityFX API, `amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll`, MIT) at native size for it to attach to, and carries the RTX 50 build of `nvngx_dlssnr.dll` next to the executable as the source of the port's weights. The NVIDIA-only files (`nvngx_dlss.dll`, `runtimes\`) are not in it.

**One-click install of the port.** Nothing of DLSS-NR-on-AMD is bundled (its terms forbid that): *Install DLSS-NR-on-AMD…* in the DLSS 5 section looks up that project's latest release, downloads its installer into the program folder and starts it; press Enter there to accept the proposed DLL name, then *Restart now*. Once it is loaded the same button reads *Update DLSS-NR-on-AMD…* and fetches its newest installer again, so updates of the port are followed without waiting for a release here. The section shows whether the FSR runtime is loaded and whether the port's DLL is in the process, and says so when the picture comes back unchanged because it is not.

**Automatic route.** *Host route* now defaults to *Automatic*: the direct route on a GeForce card, the FSR host on a Radeon card. The GeForce package (`VRChatDLSS5Cam-win64.zip`) is unchanged in what it carries and how it runs. See the new *AMD Radeon cards* section of the README (four languages) for the steps and the port's requirements (Windows 11, RX 7000 / 9000, Adrenalin 26.1.1 or newer).

**Turn and mirror the live picture.** The toolbar at the bottom of the preview now also appears for the VRChat camera (Spout) picture, with the quarter turns, the horizontal and vertical mirror and the *as it comes* button (no crop for a live source). The orientation is a setting (`spoutRotate`, `spoutFlipH`, `spoutFlipV`, also for `--set`), so the preview, the captures and the timelapse all follow it, it is kept across sessions and every change is in the history. Fixed on the way: the history entry for a turned, mirrored or cropped file showed a stray `%s`.
name: v1.4.0

body:
Pre-release: the runtime selection below has been exercised on an RTX 5090 only; reports from RTX 40 / 30 / 20 cards are welcome.

**The DLSS 5 runtime is included.** Nothing has to be supplied any more: the archive carries `nvngx_dlssnr.dll` 310.8.0.0 in two builds under `runtimes\`, `blackwell\` (the build as shipped with games, for RTX 50) and `universal\` (a community build of the same runtime adapted for RTX 40 / 30 / 20). Both files are NVIDIA's software under NVIDIA's terms and are not part of the MIT-licensed source; see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The archive is about 320 MB because of them.

**Automatic choice with fallback.** The build for the installed card is loaded at start. When it fails to load, fails to create the feature or produces a black picture for three seconds, the other build takes over, a notice says so and the choice is kept for the next start; *Reload* starts the choice over. The build in use is named next to *Runtime* in the DLSS 5 section, and the interface says so when neither build starts.

**A self-contained runtime runs without the NGX core.** The signed-snippet route no longer needs the NGX runtime when the runtime file exports its own parameter functions, which is what a build adapted for a card from another vendor would need; such a file goes into `runtimes\other\` (none is included).

**Also:** a runtime file of your own next to the executable is still honoured (tried after the bundled build for the card), any file can be selected under *Runtime path*, and updating from the application replaces the bundled builds while leaving a file of your own in place. The READMEs in the four languages describe the new layout.

body:
NVIDIA DLSS 5 neural rendering runtime (`nvngx_dlssnr.dll`), version 310.8.0.0, in the two builds that the application's release archive carries under `runtimes\`:

| Asset | Folder in the archive | Cards |
|---|---|---|
| `nvngx_dlssnr-310.8-blackwell.dll` | `runtimes\blackwell\nvngx_dlssnr.dll` | GeForce RTX 50 series (the build as shipped with games) |
| `nvngx_dlssnr-310.8-universal.dll` | `runtimes\universal\nvngx_dlssnr.dll` | GeForce RTX 40 / 30 / 20 series (community build adapted for those generations) |

These files are NVIDIA's software and remain subject to NVIDIA's terms; they are not covered by this project's MIT License. They are hosted here so that the build workflow can place them into the release archives (`gh release download runtime-310.8`), verified against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

This is not an application release: the application's releases are the `v*` tags.

body:
The first full release of the v1.2 features: everything that was in the v1.2.0 pre-release, plus the fixes below. Tested on an RTX 5090 machine.

## What is new since v1.1.0

- **Turn, mirror and crop.** A small toolbar over the preview of a library file turns it a quarter to the left or right, mirrors it horizontally or vertically, or crops it with a frame you drag (Enter applies, Esc cancels). The last button puts the file back as it came. Every file keeps its own orientation and crop, the processing and the saved result use the turned and cropped picture, and each step can be undone.
- **Your own presets.** The runtime's preset numbers, which made no visible difference, are gone. In their place the DLSS 5 section has a list of presets you create: "+" saves the current values under a name, a click applies one, and each entry can be overwritten with the current values, renamed or deleted. They live in `presets.txt` next to the settings.
- **Search the settings.** A field at the top of the sidebar filters the controls by name; only the matching ones and their sections stay visible. Esc or the ✕ clears it.
- **Smooth wipe on slow videos.** The compare wipe follows the mouse at the interface's own frame rate; it no longer waits for the next processed video frame.
- **One bar on each side.** The sidebar and the library are folded by a click on their bar, and resized by dragging the thin line along the bar's inner edge — the line turns blue and the pointer becomes a resize arrow, so the two never share the same spot.
- **Fades.** Switching between Live, Picture and Video, entering and leaving fullscreen, and the main window after the start-up card all fade instead of cutting. The library stays put while the picture fades.
- **Explorer-like selection.** A click on the library's empty space clears the selection.
- **Help in one click.** The "?" button in the top bar (and "Documentation" in About) opens the guide in the interface's language.
- **Reopen the last file** is now a switch in the Display section and is off by default (`reopenLast` on the command line).

## Fixed since the v1.2.0 pre-release

- The bars no longer mix click and drag: the bar itself folds the panel (hand pointer), and only the line at its edge resizes it.
- The rounded corners where the sidebar's bar and the library's bar meet left a small gap; both bars and the panels around them are now flush.
- The fade when switching between Live, Picture and Video covered the library as well; it now covers only the picture.

## Notes

- Requirements are unchanged (Windows 10/11, GeForce RTX, the DLSS 5 runtime DLL supplied by you).
- Settings and the library from earlier versions are kept; the old preset number is ignored.

body:
Pre-release: the new features below were checked on one RTX 5090 machine only. v1.0.0 stays the release for everyday use.

## What is new

- **Turn, mirror and crop.** A small toolbar over the preview of a library file turns it a quarter to the left or right, mirrors it horizontally or vertically, or crops it with a frame you drag (Enter applies, Esc cancels). The last button puts the file back as it came. Every file keeps its own orientation and crop, the processing and the saved result use the turned and cropped picture, and each step can be undone.
- **Your own presets.** The runtime's preset numbers, which made no visible difference, are gone. In their place the DLSS 5 section has a list of presets you create: "+" saves the current values under a name, a click applies one, and each entry can be overwritten with the current values, renamed or deleted. They live in `presets.txt` next to the settings.
- **Search the settings.** A field at the top of the sidebar filters the controls by name; only the matching ones and their sections stay visible. Esc or the ✕ clears it.
- **Smooth wipe on slow videos.** The compare wipe follows the mouse at the interface's own frame rate; it no longer waits for the next processed video frame.
- **One bar on each side.** The sidebar's handle and the library's top edge are now the same kind of long bar: a click hides or shows (folds or unfolds), a drag resizes, and the moving edge lights up blue under the mouse. The library header's fold button is gone.
- **Fades.** Switching between Live, Picture and Video, entering and leaving fullscreen, and the main window after the start-up card all fade instead of cutting.
- **Explorer-like selection.** A click on the library's empty space clears the selection.
- **Help in one click.** The "?" button in the top bar (and "Documentation" in About) opens the guide in the interface's language.
- **Start-up card.** It shows the version and a "Pre-release" tag on pre-release builds; the main window fades in once its first frame is ready.
- **Reopen the last file** is now a switch in the Display section and is off by default (`reopenLast` on the command line).

## Notes

- Requirements are unchanged (Windows 10/11, GeForce RTX, the DLSS 5 runtime DLL supplied by you).
- Settings and the library from earlier versions are kept; the old preset number is ignored.
